title: Piki makes billions, Gabby loses billions: Lopez Holdings takes ₱1.8B Q3 hit as Meralco shares tank

 Piki makes billions, Gabby loses billions: Lopez Holdings takes ₱1.8B Q3 hit as Meralco shares tank 
 Bilyonaryo Federico “Piki” Lopez's power empire is making billions, while estranged cousin Eugenio “Gabby” Lopez III's ABS-CBN continues to pile up losses. 
 November 17, 2026 • 
 7:33 PM 
 Share
 By Bilyonaryo staff 
 Bilyonaryo Federico “Piki” Lopez’s power empire is making billions, while estranged cousin Eugenio “Gabby” Lopez III’s ABS-CBN continues to pile up losses. But even with profits rolling in, their family’s listed holding company has taken a multibillion-peso hit from a familiar investment: Meralco.
 Lopez Holdings Corp. recorded a ₱1.78 billion third-quarter comprehensive loss attributable to shareholders, reversing a ₱3.34 billion gain a year earlier, despite an 18 percent increase in net profit attributable to shareholders to ₱2.53 billion.
 The setback coincided with a 27 percent plunge in Manila Electric Co. (Meralco) shares, which fell to ₱416.60 at the end of September from ₱570 at the end of June.
 The Lopez group retains a 3.95 percent stake in Meralco, equivalent to approximately 44.38 million shares. 
 Based on the ₱153.40 decline in Meralco’s share price, the investment lost an estimated ₱6.81 billion in market value during the quarter. Meralco’s selloff accelerated in July after President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. proposed scrapping system-loss charges from electricity bills, raising concerns about the power distributor’s future earnings.
 Lopez Holdings and its subsidiaries reported ₱6.82 billion in unrealized investment valuation losses, net of tax, during the period. 
 The amount closely matches the estimated decline in the Meralco stake’s market value, although the company did not attribute the entire loss specifically to Meralco.
 These paper losses did not involve an equivalent cash outflow or reduce reported net profit. Instead, they were reflected in comprehensive income, helping push Lopez Holdings to a ₱1.78 billion comprehensive loss attributable to shareholders after other adjustments.
 The setback comes amid contrasting performances by the businesses associated with the two estranged Lopez cousins.
 Piki’s First Philippine Holdings (FPH) saw revenue surge 61 percent to ₱94.34 billion in the first nine months of 2026 from ₱58.77 billion a year earlier, driven largely by electricity sales.
 The power and property conglomerate earned ₱13.40 billion in net income attributable to shareholders, up 7 percent, while recurring profit rose 9 percent to ₱13.4 billion.
 Gabby’s ABS-CBN, meanwhile, remained deep in the red.
 The broadcaster’s nine-month revenue fell 11 percent to ₱10.52 billion, while its net loss widened 32 percent to ₱2.96 billion from ₱2.24 billion.
 The contrasting fortunes follow a bitter family feud over a proposed ₱2 billion funding injection into ABS-CBN, which Piki opposed.
 The feud led to an unsuccessful attempt to oust Piki as Lopez Inc. president. Gabby’s family later sold its stake in the holding company, with Gabby acquiring direct stakes in ABS-CBN and Rockwell Land.
 Despite ABS-CBN’s mounting losses, Lopez Holdings earned ₱8.05 billion in net income attributable to shareholders during the first nine months, up 7 percent from ₱7.49 billion a year earlier.
 The group also benefited from ₱5.46 billion in earnings from equity-accounted investments, largely reflecting First Gen’s retained interest in its natural gas business following a 2025 transaction with companies controlled by trilyonaryo Enrique Razon Jr.’s Prime Infrastructure.
 But investment valuation losses overshadowed much of the group’s improved earnings.
 For the first nine months, comprehensive income attributable to Lopez Holdings shareholders plunged 67 percent to ₱3.19 billion from ₱9.56 billion a year earlier. —Bilyonaryo.com
